messages:
alert-bot: [SECURITY] Public GCS bucket detected: gs://prod-backups-2026 — ACL contains allUsers (scanner: bucket-acl-scan)
noah (cloud-sec): Heads-up — scanner flagged backups bucket as public. paging infra/oncall. Can someone confirm quickly?
maria (sec-eng): @alex can you run an acl check and kms policy check? If it's public we should remove access and rotate keys asap.
alex (infra): Running quick checks now.
alex (infra): `gsutil acl get gs://prod-backups-2026` -> shows `allUsers: READER` on bucket root. Also `gsutil ls -L gs://prod-backups-2026 | head` shows listing of files (backup-*.tar.gz).
alex (infra): Also ran `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/backup-kr/cryptoKeys/backup-key` -> there's a binding with `members: - allAuthenticatedUsers` and role `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter`.
kai (eng-sre): yikes. That KMS binding explains why backups could be decrypted by non-org clients if they had the blobs. Priorities: 1) block public access to bucket 2) remove broad KMS binding 3) rotate keys 4) check backups for sensitive PII
maria (sec-eng): Agreed. Execution plan: alex to block bucket, noah to remove KMS binding, kai to rotate key and suspend any CI jobs using it, lin to coordinate comms to owners, i'll open an incident and set severity.
alex (infra): Blocking bucket now: `gsutil acl ch -d AllUsers gs://prod-backups-2026` -> done, ACL no longer shows allUsers. Also applied a temporary uniform bucket-level access: `gsutil uniformbucketlevelaccess set on gs://prod-backups-2026` to prevent object ACL re-add.
noah (cloud-sec): Removing KMS binding: `gcloud kms keys remove-iam-policy-binding projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/backup-kr/cryptoKeys/backup-key --member=allAuthenticatedUsers --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` -> succeeded. Added org policy check to detect any future allAuthenticatedUsers bindings.
rotator-bot: Started key rotation job for backup-key -> rotation job queued (job id rot-20260320-1). Will create new key version and mark old versions disabled after verification.
kai (eng-sre): Paused CI pipelines referencing `projects/redwood/.../backup-key` in secure vault. Asked infra to rotate any service account keys used by CI that might have accessed the key.
alex (infra): Confirmed pausing deploys. Listed objects access logs: `gsutil logging get gs://prod-backups-2026` shows read activity from 3 external IPs in last 30 days. Exporting access logs to investigations bucket.
maria (sec-eng): Opened incident INC-2026-42, severity: high (sensitive backups exposed). Notifying legal and customer-success for potential disclosure assessment. Lin, can you draft the internal comms and external checklist?
lin (product-security): On it. Drafting message: internal owners + exec summary + actions done + ETA for key rotation and audit. Will post to #all-hands and send to affected product leads after legal review.
noah (cloud-sec): Quick triage notes: - Public reads documented, unknown if any file contents were downloaded. - KMS binding allowed decryption by outside accounts with ciphertext; need to assume compromise until proven otherwise. - Start integrity checks on backups (hashes) and compare to last-known-good.
kai (eng-sre): Running content sampling and hash comparison. If backups contain customer PII we escalate to legal and CS for notifications.
alex (infra): Exported list of objects and checksums: `gsutil ls -L gs://prod-backups-2026 | awk '/Hash/ {print $2}' > /tmp/backup_hashes.txt` and pushed to investigations bucket with restricted ACL.
maria (sec-eng): Post-incident immediate actions to add to ticket: 1) Confirm no external downloads (analyze access logs) 2) Rotate KMS key and revoke old key versions 3) Rotate any SA keys used by CI 4) Add alert for any bucket ACL containing AllUsers/allAuthenticatedUsers 5) Add CI guardrail preventing public bucket creation 6) Update runbook
rotator-bot: Key rotation complete: new version v2 created, v1 disabled. Please validate decryption with new version and then revoke old key versions.
kai (eng-sre): Validation: decryption test passed against a sample object using new key version.
maria (sec-eng): Next: schedule 1-2 hour postmortem meeting tomorrow. Owners: infra (alex), eng-sre (kai), sec-eng (maria), cloud-sec (noah), product-security (lin). Tasks assigned in ticket INC-2026-42.
lin (product-security): Also proposing a short policy change: deny `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` to `allAuthenticatedUsers` and flag any membership that isn't a named service account or Google group.
noah (cloud-sec): I'll add a GCP org policy + continuous scanner rule. Also creating an audit log alert for any IAM binding changes on cryptoKeys.
alex (infra): Added terraform change to enforce uniform bucket-level access, and a presubmit lint that fails if bucket resource has `predefinedAcl = "publicRead"`.
maria (sec-eng): Thanks everyone. Keep updates in the incident ticket. We'll reconvene after the forensic log analysis. Quick wins done: bucket privatized, broad KMS binding removed, key rotated, CI paused. Remaining: log analysis for downloads, customer impact assessment, postmortem writeup.
lin (product-security): Draft comms complete; waiting on legal. Will share in the incident channel when cleared.
alert-bot: Incident INC-2026-42 created and linked. Severity: high. Pager duty: notified oncall.
